attributes.action: Require safe, reliable gluten-free meals for people with coeliac disease
attributes.additional_details: People with coeliac disease need to avoid gluten and cross-contamination, yet eating out can be extremely difficult. Families often have to research restaurants in advance, travel long distances and still cannot be certain that advertised gluten-free food is available or safely prepared. My daughter has coeliac disease and we have experienced this first-hand, including being left without a meal when a gluten-free option advertised was not actually available.
attributes.background: Require restaurants and food outlets to provide at least one safe, clearly identified gluten-free meal suitable for people with coeliac disease, with measures to prevent gluten cross-contamination and accurate information about availability.

rejection.details:
Your petition is about something that the Scottish Government and Scottish Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it. 

The Scottish Parliament has its own Public Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Scottish Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.parliament.scot/

You may also wish to contact your local council and MSP who represent you about this issue. 

You can find the name of your local council and how to contact them here: https://www.mygov.scot/find-your-local-council

You can find the name of your local MSP and how to contact them here: https://www.parliament.scot/msps

You may also be interested in the work of Food Standards Scotland, which was established under the Food (Scotland) Act 2015 as the new public sector food body for Scotland: https://www.foodstandards.gov.scot/
